mission.title: cert-manager: Allowing skipping HTTP01 and DNS01 self-check on a per-solver basis
mission.description: Allowing skipping HTTP01 and DNS01 self-check on a per-solver basis. Requested by 87+ users.

steps.title: Check current cert-manager deployment
steps.description:
Verify your cert-manager version and configuration:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n cert-manager -l app.kubernetes.io/name=cert-manager
helm list -n cert-manager 2>/dev/null || echo "Not installed via Helm"
```
This feature requires a working cert-manager installation.

steps.title: Review cert-manager configuration
steps.description:
Inspect the relevant cert-manager configuration:
```bash
kubectl get all -n cert-manager -l app.kubernetes.io/name=cert-manager
kubectl get configmap -n cert-manager -l app.kubernetes.io/part-of=cert-manager
```
Kinda intercects with #863, in nat nets cant successfully self validate acme rules, because of local k8s providers, which  refuses to create hairpin nat

Nice env variable or cmd-flag for skip local self check and leave it up to the user

steps.title: Verify the feature works
steps.description:
Test that the new capability is working as expected:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n cert-manager -l app.kubernetes.io/name=cert-manager
kubectl get events -n cert-manager --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | tail -10
```
Confirm the feature described in "Allowing skipping HTTP01 and DNS01 self-check on a…" is functioning correctly.

resolution.summary:
This has been discussed before and we've avoided allowing it as we need *some* way to ensure that the challenge has propagated.

For DNS01, options like `--dns01-recursive-nameservers` and `--dns01-recursive-nameservers-only` help users that have DNS restricted environments that use DNS01.

prerequisites.description: A running Kubernetes cluster with cert-manager installed or the issue environment reproducible.
